correctness.summary: For any induced subgraph meeting both factors, pseudoforest sparsity bounds its edge count by a two-variable rational density whose discrete differences are nonnegative except at one-vertex boundary cases when both factors are unicyclic; the exact one-vertex edge count resolves those cases. One-factor subgraphs are strictly sparser. Nash--Williams then gives the arboricity formula. A separate monotonicity argument proves the independent-set extension. Exhaustive small-graph checks agree in all 631 tested instances.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: The 2026 Kuanyshov--Yeginbay source proves only general bounds for joins and computes complete bipartite graphs, fans, one path--independent-set example, and wheels; it does not state arbitrary pseudotree formulas. Searches under join/sum and 1-balanced/uniformly-dense terminology found no equivalent theorem. The main residual risk is Hobbs--Kannan--Lai--Lai--Weng (2010): inspected publisher text concerns generalized Cartesian products of equal-size modules, and some equal-order tree-join special cases may be derivable there, but the complete article was not checked line-by-line. No concrete prior coverage of the arbitrary-order pseudotree and unicyclic formulas was found.

value.summary: The theorem converts a recent join-arboricity bound into an exact, shape-independent formula for a broad sparse class. It identifies joins of pseudotrees as whole-graph density extremizers and simultaneously subsumes the recent fan, wheel, and path--independent-set examples while extending them to all trees and unicyclic graphs.

limitations: Disconnected pseudoforests and connected graphs of larger cyclomatic number are not classified.
The independent-set extension has only one pseudotree factor.
The complete 2010 1-balanced-construction article was not checked line-by-line.
Finite verification supports but does not replace the proof.
Independent audit has not been performed.
